strategyName: Dual Momentum - One-Rebalance Winner Grace v1
researchQuestion: Does giving an outgoing profitable incumbent exactly one additional monthly rebalance period improve canonical Dual Momentum without sacrificing useful loser replacement behavior?

configuration.universe: registered EQUITY_UNIVERSE resolved through the Dow point-in-time membership ledger
configuration.ranking: 189-session close-to-close trailing return; qualify only above the run-window risk-free rate
configuration.positionSizing: equal weight across selected names, maximum five positions
configuration.transactionCosts: the canonical per-symbol spread estimates plus the registered commission assumption
configuration.decisionTiming: history strictly before the rebalance session

developmentPeriod.reason: The completed Trade Lifecycle / Exit-Efficiency Audit inspected this full period for winner exits and replacement behavior. No clean historical holdout remains and none will be manufactured by relabeling inspected dates.

primaryModification.name: One-Rebalance Winner Grace
primaryModification.winnerDefinition: At the pre-open rebalance decision timestamp, the last close available strictly before the rebalance session divided by the incumbent's actual lifecycle entry-open price minus one is strictly positive. The current rebalance open remains the execution price and is not used to decide eligibility because it is not yet known.
rule: Compute the canonical qualifying top-five ranking without alteration.
A currently held name outside that canonical target is an outgoing incumbent.

If its last point-in-time close is strictly above its actual lifecycle entry-open price and it did not receive grace at the immediately preceding rebalance, retain it for exactly one additional rebalance period.
If multiple outgoing incumbents qualify, retain them in ascending current canonical momentum rank, with unrankable names last and symbol as the deterministic final tie-break.

Fill every remaining invested slot, in canonical rank order, from the normal canonical target, excluding retained grace names. On ordinary five-name rebalances portfolio capacity remains five; no sixth name, leverage, or additional capital is allowed. If the canonical absolute-momentum filter supplies fewer than five names, the modified target preserves that canonical invested-slot count and cash allocation; grace is limited to the number of actual canonical incoming names available to defer.

The canonical incoming name displaced from the fifth slot upward by each grace retention is the deferred incoming for event accounting, paired in retained-incumbent rank order against displaced names in canonical rank order.

At the next rebalance the grace expires. If the incumbent is independently in the canonical top five it becomes a normal holding; otherwise it exits and cannot receive chained grace for that exit event.
Zero-return and losing outgoing incumbents never receive grace and exit on the canonical schedule.
primaryModification.state: Track actual lifecycle entry price and a one-period grace-active flag per held security. Reset the flag only after the security independently returns to the canonical target or exits.

capacityAndExecution.targetPositions: five when five names pass the canonical absolute filter; otherwise exactly the canonical target count, preserving canonical cash slots
capacityAndExecution.weights: equal weights using the canonical engine's target-weight convention; 20% when five securities are available, with canonical cash behavior preserved if fewer than five names qualify
capacityAndExecution.priceForWinnerState: last close strictly before the rebalance session versus actual lifecycle entry open; the current open is reserved for execution
capacityAndExecution.futureEventWindow: current rebalance open through next rebalance open for both incumbent and deferred incoming
capacityAndExecution.costs: apply canonical costs to actual modified-strategy traded deltas; counterfactual event returns are gross price comparisons over identical windows

metrics.primary: Mean incumbent-minus-deferred-incoming open-to-open return over the next rebalance period
secondary: median event difference and event win rate
net cumulative return, CAGR, annualized volatility, Sharpe, Sortino, max drawdown and drawdown duration
worst day, rolling 5 sessions, rolling 20 sessions, worst month and positive-month share
turnover, costs, average completed-position holding period, entries and exits
winner MFE capture, winner giveback, post-exit continuation, replacement quality
concentration, pairwise correlation, sector concentration where point-in-time labels are usable

dependenceAndRobustness.effectiveN: unique rebalance dates containing at least one grace event
dependenceAndRobustness.null: zero mean incumbent-minus-deferred return; uncertainty is descriptive because no clean holdout remains
dependenceAndRobustness.concentration: top 1, top 3 and top 5 event contributions plus leave-one-rebalance-cluster-out mean and cumulative event impact

historicalCandidateRequiresForwardValida: mean and median grace-event incumbent-minus-deferred return are positive
modified net cumulative return exceeds canonical control
winner capture improves or winner giveback declines
max drawdown deterioration is no more than 2 percentage points and worst-day deterioration is no more than 1 percentage point
at least 12 independent grace rebalance clusters
the largest single grace event supplies less than 50% of total positive event contribution
successCriteria.interestingHistoricalCandidateInsufficie: Mechanism economics are positive but one or more breadth, risk, lifecycle, or effective-N criteria fail.
successCriteria.modificationUnsupported: Primary mean event economics are non-positive, net portfolio performance declines, loser replacement is not preserved, or tail-risk deterioration exceeds a preregistered limit without commensurate mechanism evidence.
successCriteria.validationPassed: Unavailable on this historical sample because no genuinely unseen validation slice remains.

preResultAmendments.stage: first execution stopped before any modified performance result was produced
preResultAmendments.issue: Canonical DM held only two qualifying names on 2022-10-03. Requiring five modified holdings would either admit three absolute-momentum failures or grace non-winners, violating higher-priority frozen rules.
preResultAmendments.resolution: Preserve the canonical invested-slot count and cash allocation whenever fewer than five names qualify. Grace events require and are capped by actual canonical incoming names, so every event retains the intended incumbent-versus-deferred-incoming counterfactual.
